clue.text: Evidence of a slack washer

parts.note: someone who washes carelessly leaves a grimy line round the bath or neck; slack also hints at slack water at the turn of the sea

explanation.surface: Proof that somebody has been lazy at their ablutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slack' suggests slack water between ebb and flow, nudging the solver towards the sea before the bathroom reading lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the ring of dirt left on a bath or on skin by poor washing.

clue.text: A little short of words at mess

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Slightly lacking vocabulary at the dinner table in the officers' mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching but not yet reaching, as in getting near midnight.

clue.text: List of people to run Circle Line

parts.note: to run an organisation is to direct it
O is round like a circle
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A roster of staff appointed to manage a London Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a book giving names and addresses, such as a telephone book.

clue.text: Running across junction

explanation.surface: A sprinter dashes over a crossroads.
explanation.definitionFit: Running across someone is encountering them by chance; a junction is where roads or rivers join.

clue.text: Turn red saying why split up nearly came

indicators.note: in a down entry, up signals the word for split is read from the bottom
nearly means almost all, so the final letter of the word for split is dropped

parts.note: a split is a fissure, a crack

indicators.note: saying signals the word for why is spoken, giving a letter with that name

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like why

explanation.surface: Someone blushes, explaining why a couple separated and almost reconciled.
explanation.walkthrough: FISSURE without its last letter is FISSUR; 'up' turns it to RUSSIF. 'Saying' gives Y from why. 'Came' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Red stands for communist, and to Russify is to make something Russian, as Soviet policy did.

clue.text: No horns for this composer

explanation.surface: A musician with an unusual dislike of brass instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a hummel beast is a hornless one, and Johann Nepomuk Hummel was an Austrian composer and pianist.

clue.text: Induce well-off subject to remember

parts.note: a trance-inducer sends a subject well off into sleep and then coaxes buried memories out

explanation.surface: Persuade a wealthy citizen to keep something in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-off' suggests rich, but here a subject goes well off into a trance; 'subject' is the person on the couch.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypnotise is to put a person into a trance in which they respond to suggestion and may recall forgotten events.

clue.text: He is still using Veronica in his performance

definitions.text: He is still using Veronica in his performance

parts.words: He is still using Veronica in his performance
parts.note: a veronica is a bullfighting pass in which the cape is swung slowly while the fighter keeps his feet planted

explanation.surface: An actor who goes on relying on a woman called Veronica in his act.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica looks like a woman's name, but it is the classic cape pass in a bullfight.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who works the bull with the cape and kills it.

clue.text: Stop — amber changing to green light

indicators.note: changing means altering, so the letters of amber are rearranged

parts.note: a green traffic light means go

explanation.surface: A driver halts as the traffic lights move from amber to green.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban that halts trade or publication.

clue.text: Phew! drains off in Septimus Harding's office

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Relief as plumbing problems are cleared away in a cathedral official's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Septimus Harding is the title character of Trollope's novel The Warden, a gentle clergyman who holds the post of warden of a charitable hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Harding's post in Trollope's novel is that of warden, so his office is the position held by a warden.

clue.text: This is blown over border

indicators.note: over signals that the word for border is turned the other way round

parts.note: to border is to abut, lying alongside

explanation.surface: Something carried by the wind across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuba is a large brass instrument played by blowing into its mouthpiece.

clue.text: Accepting regime that makes a firm bust

parts.note: accepting something is receiving it
a regime is a system or order of things

explanation.surface: A government that welcomes all comers soon bankrupts business.
explanation.definitionFit: A receiving order is the court order placing a debtor's affairs with an official receiver, the step in bankruptcy proceedings.

clue.text: Muddy lake in outskirts of Salisbury

indicators.note: in places the Irish word for lake within the letters taken from the city's name
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters of Salisbury are used

parts.note: a lough is an Irish lake

explanation.surface: A boggy pond on the edge of a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Salisbury are S and Y, and LOUGH goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloughy describes ground like a slough, a miry swamp full of mud.

clue.text: Passion over English king's unenlightenment

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: heat is intensity of feeling, passion
Henry was the name of eight English kings

explanation.surface: Ardour beats the wisdom of a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathenry is the state of being heathen, a pagan ignorance of true religion.

clue.text: He looks pale in promenade concert

definitions.text: He looks pale in promenade concert

parts.words: He looks pale in promenade concert
parts.note: the whitened face of a traditional seaside clown, who performed in troupes in shows on the pier

explanation.surface: An ashen-faced man attending a Prom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promenade concert' suggests the London Proms, but the promenade here is the seaside pier where white-faced clown troupes gave concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a clown in loose white costume and whitened face, a staple of Edwardian seaside entertainment.

clue.text: Stern warning from saloon-proprietor at night

definitions.text: Stern warning from saloon-proprietor at night

parts.words: Stern warning from saloon-proprietor at night
parts.note: the owner of a saloon car shows a red lamp at the stern of the vehicle after dark to warn traffic behind

explanation.surface: A landlord sternly calls time at his pub late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon-proprietor' suggests a publican, but a saloon is also a car, and stern means its back end.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear light is the red lamp at the back of a vehicle, alerting following drivers.

clue.text: Useful part of mission, to discharge worry

parts.note: to discharge a debt is to pay it
a worry is a load on one's mind

explanation.surface: An envoy is sent on a mission to settle a troubling debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The payload is the cargo or warheads a rocket or aircraft carries, the part that does the job of the flight.

clue.text: Bearing left in Luton, for example

parts.note: one's bearing is one's air or manner
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A traveller heads off in a direction away from a Bedfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton, a town north of London, is home to one of London's airports.
explanation.definitionFit: Luton has a major passenger terminal for flights, so it is one example of a place where aircraft land.

clue.text: An oil spread in between ends of Lincoln?

definitions.text: An oil spread in between ends of Lincoln?

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters between the outside letters of the city name
ends are the first and last letters, so only those of Lincoln are used
spread about means scattered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grease rubbed on, perhaps from Lincoln sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' turns AN OIL into ANOLI, which goes between L and N, the first and last letters of Lincoln. The whole clue also defines it, Lincoln being a breed of woolly sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy substance from sheep's wool, used as an ointment base.

clue.text: Tenable variety of May Day celebration

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A defensible choice among the festivities of spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Beltane is the old Celtic festival held on the first of May, marked by bonfires.

clue.text: Money that is found in old golf-bag

parts.note: brass is slang for money
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Cash discovered in an antique set of clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie was an old wooden golf club with a brass sole plate, roughly a two-wood.

clue.text: Some rank play by forwards

parts.note: in rugby the forwards stand in a row to contest the ball thrown in from touch

explanation.surface: Dreadful acting by pushy people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' suggests foul, but here it is a row of players; rugby forwards form two such rows at a throw-in.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineout is the rugby set-piece restarting play after the ball goes into touch.

clue.text: Charm of the nineteenth, rallying-point

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The appeal of the nineteenth hole as the clubhouse gathering place.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone is to captivate or delight them.

clue.text: Get into the hit parade?

parts.note: read the parade literally as two lines of people striking whoever passes between them

explanation.surface: A singer hopes to land a record in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit parade' means the pop charts, but here it is a parade of hitters, the old punishment of passing between two rows of men with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: To run the gauntlet was to pass between two rows of men who struck the victim, now meaning to face attack or criticism.

clue.text: Monkshood, a cure for smoking?

explanation.surface: A poisonous plant suggested as a remedy for a nicotine habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood worn by a friar is one sense; the other is the revolving chimney cap that stops a fireplace belching smoke.

clue.text: Retailer of spicy items

parts.note: a seller of hot goods is really someone who passes on juicy gossip and stories

explanation.surface: A grocer stocking hot peppers and chillies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retailer' suggests a shop, but to retail a story is to repeat it, and spicy items are titbits of scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsmonger is a gossip who eagerly spreads rumours and tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Nettle in front of you is close

indicators.note: puts the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: to nettle is to irritate, sting
Y is a short form of you, as in informal writing

explanation.surface: A stinging plant right in your path is very near.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of mean with money, unwilling to spend.

clue.text: Small pile of sand needs sweeping to get dry

parts.note: golfers once teed up the ball on a pinch of sand before wooden pegs were used
sweeping means complete, all-out, as in a total victory

explanation.surface: A heap of sand on the floor must be brushed away before it dries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' is not the opposite of wet but describes someone who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry person or area is one where alcohol is forbidden, the abstinent sense.
